name: Stinging nettle
caution: A sting is not an identification test. Do not eat raw stinging foliage.

name: Dandelion
caution: Sap may irritate skin. Food use does not establish the safety or effectiveness of concentrated products.

name: Common yarrow
caution: Can cause contact dermatitis. Do not identify by a flat white flower cluster alone.

name: Black elder
caution: Raw or unripe berries and leaves or stems contain cyanide-producing substances. Do not use them.

name: American wild mint
caution: Pennyroyal is also a mint and is harmful if eaten. Hybrids complicate identification.

name: Red clover
caution: Check with a clinician before herbal use, especially during pregnancy, breastfeeding or when taking medicines.

name: Greater plantain
caution: Road margins, sprayed paths and pet-used lawns are poor gathering sites.

name: Mugwort
caution: NCCIH advises against use during pregnancy. Evidence for claimed health effects is limited.

name: Dog rose
caution: Wild roses are difficult to separate. Avoid ornamental shrubs with an unknown spray history.

name: Lemon balm
caution: Scent alone does not identify a plant. Confirm leaf arrangement and flowers as well.

name: German chamomile
caution: Allergic reactions can be severe, especially with daisy-family allergies. Medicine interactions are possible.

name: Calendula
caution: The common name marigold also refers to Tagetes. Ornamental nursery plants may have unsuitable pesticide treatments.

name: Wild garlic
caution: Lily of the valley and autumn crocus can grow among ramsons. Garlic scent transferred to hands can mislead.

name: Common purslane
caution: Contains oxalates; avoid large intakes. Rule out spurges before any food use.

name: Common chickweed
caution: Avoid mixing several groundcover species. Flowerless fragments are especially easy to confuse.

name: Yellow wood sorrel
caution: Large amounts can be harmful because of oxalates. Sour taste is never an identification test.

name: Sheep sorrel
caution: Contains substantial oxalic acid. Do not taste uncertain arrow-shaped leaves.

name: Garlic mustard
caution: A garlic smell alone cannot identify it. Do not spread mature seed during collection.

name: Cleavers
caution: Other bedstraws differ chemically. Do not infer edibility from a sticky stem.

name: Fennel
caution: Carrot-family mistakes can be fatal. Do not gather an unknown umbellifer by smell.

name: Watercress
caution: Wild watercress can carry liver flukes and contaminants. Clear water and rinsing do not establish safety.

name: Selfheal
caution: The common name heal-all is historical language, not evidence of medical effectiveness.

name: Common blue violet
caution: Do not identify a plant from a heart-shaped leaf alone. Ornamental African violets are unrelated.

name: Gotu kola
caution: Wild wet-ground plants can be contaminated. Food use is not evidence for concentrated supplements or treatment claims.

name: Lemongrass
caution: Other Cymbopogon species are grown for fragrance or oils. A lemon scent does not make them interchangeable.

name: Roselle
caution: Do not substitute ornamental hibiscus or identify by a red flower alone.

name: Moringa
caution: This entry covers food parts only. Do not infer that roots, bark, extracts or water-treatment claims are safe.

name: Culantro
caution: Leaf edges and flowering bracts can be sharp. It is not the same species as coriander.

name: Epazote
caution: Seeds in quantity and concentrated preparations can be dangerous. This guide supplies no home remedy or dose.

name: Lemon verbena
caution: Several plants are called verbena or yerba luisa. Do not substitute on the common name alone.

name: Perilla
caution: Color and aroma alone do not identify perilla. Keep it out of livestock grazing areas.

name: Warrigal greens
caution: Contains oxalic acid; do not present it as a raw salad green or unrestricted spinach substitute.

name: Lemon myrtle
caution: Other aromatic rainforest trees can resemble it. Confirm a named plant before use.

name: Kapokbos
caution: The name wild rosemary covers unrelated plants. Do not substitute it for culinary rosemary or ingest oils.

name: Rooibos
caution: Do not identify or harvest an unfamiliar fynbos shrub by needlelike leaves alone.

name: Round-leaf buchu
caution: Related buchus differ chemically. A traditional name does not identify a species or establish safety.

name: Poison hemlock
caution: All parts are highly poisonous. Small amounts can be fatal; obtain urgent poison-service advice after exposure.

name: Spotted water hemlock
caution: All parts are toxic and ingestion can be fatal. Seek urgent poison-service advice.

name: Lily of the valley
caution: Can cause serious poisoning including heart-rhythm disturbances. Seek prompt poison-service advice after ingestion.

name: Autumn crocus
caution: Colchicine poisoning can be fatal and symptoms may be delayed. Do not wait for illness before seeking help.

name: Foxglove
caution: Cardiac glycosides can cause serious, potentially fatal poisoning. Seek urgent advice after ingestion.

name: Pennyroyal
caution: The RHS explicitly identifies pennyroyal as non-edible and harmful if eaten.

name: Spotted spurge
caution: Sap can injure skin and eyes; ingestion irritates the mouth and digestive tract.

name: Common comfrey
caution: Ingestion can damage the liver. A history of medicinal use does not establish safety.
